note: Patterns, word lists and examples are original wording. 'better' contains no invented figures, studies or names; placeholders are in square brackets.

contrast: \b(?:it['’]s|it is|this is|that['’]s|that is|it was)\s+not\s+(?:just\s+|only\s+|really\s+)?(?:about\s+)?[^.!?;\n]{1,60}[.;,]\s*(?:it['’]s|it is|this is|that['’]s|it was)\b
lexicon.heading_label: ^\s*(?:conclusion|in conclusion|introduction|intro|summary|in summary|final thoughts|closing thoughts|wrapping up|wrap-up|overview|key takeaways|the bottom line|tl;dr)\s*[.!:]?\s*$

patterns.name: Figure without a source
patterns.description: Percentages, shares, amounts, large numbers or multiples with no source in the same sentence. Measurements, years, versions, legal sections and times do not count.
patterns.bad: 73% of customers read reviews before buying.
patterns.better: A link to the survey in the same sentence, or: At our shop, [your number from your own experience] out of ten customers ask about reviews first.
patterns.fix: Add the source as a link or (source: name) in the same sentence, mark the figure as your own experience, or cut it.

patterns.name: Vague attribution
patterns.description: "Studies show", "experts say", "according to a survey": an authority is invoked but not named.
patterns.bad: Studies show that short texts work better.
patterns.better: Name the study with a link, or write what you observed yourself: [your observation].

match.pattern: (?<!\bour )(?<!\bmy )(?<!\byour )\b(?:(?:recent|new|numerous|many|several|various|some|multiple) )?(?:studies|research|surveys|statistics|analyses|data|findings|reports) (?:show|shows|suggest|suggests|prove|proves|indicate|indicates|confirm|confirms|reveal|reveals|has shown|have shown|found|demonstrate|demonstrates)\b|\b(?:(?:many|most|leading|some|top|industry) )?(?:experts|specialists|researchers|scientists|analysts|insiders|marketers) (?:agree|say|said|believe|recommend|warn|suggest|estimate|predict|argue|claim)\b|\baccording to (?:experts|researchers|research|studies|a (?:recent |new )?(?:study|survey|report|poll|analysis)|analysts|recent research|industry experts|many experts)\b|\b(?:a|one) (?:recent|new|large|landmark|groundbreaking) (?:study|survey|report|poll|analysis)\b|\bscientifically proven\b|\bresearch has (?:shown|found|proven)\b

patterns.fix: Name and link the source, or rewrite the sentence as your own experience.

patterns.name: Person without a source
patterns.description: A named person is quoted or paraphrased without a source in the sentence. Check that the person exists and said this.
patterns.bad: Marketing expert Thomas Weber says content is everything.
patterns.better: [Name] told us on [date]: "[exact quote]", or a link to the original source.
patterns.fix: Add a link to the original source or cut the person. Allow your own name with the config key own_names.

patterns.name: Interchangeable paragraph
patterns.description: A longer paragraph without a single concrete detail: no number, name, place, date, example or first-hand experience. It could appear in any text on the topic.
patterns.bad: Good communication is the basis of all collaboration. Those who communicate clearly avoid misunderstandings and build trust.
patterns.better: Add one detail only you know: [a case from your work, with a place or time].
patterns.fix: Add one concrete detail from your own experience or cut the paragraph.

patterns.name: Little concrete detail
patterns.description: Across the whole text there are very few concrete details per 100 words (numbers, names, dates, examples, first-hand experience). Threshold is provisional.
patterns.bad: A whole article made of general advice.
patterns.better: At least one example from your practice per section: [case], [time span], [result].
patterns.fix: Add your own cases, sourced figures and examples.

patterns.name: Advice without steps
patterns.description: A paragraph piles up instructions ("you should", "make sure") but gives neither steps nor an example.
patterns.bad: You should know your audience. You should post regularly. Make sure to focus on quality.
patterns.better: A numbered list of the steps you actually take, with one example: [step 1], [step 2].
patterns.fix: Break the advice into steps or add an example from practice.

patterns.name: Smoothed-over detail
patterns.description: A concrete detail is replaced by a vague one: "a leading provider", "well-known companies", "numerous clients".
patterns.bad: A leading company already uses the method.
patterns.better: Name the company if you may, or describe it: [industry], [size], [what they do with it].
patterns.fix: Name it, or describe the detail that makes the case specific.

patterns.name: Figure from your own experience
patterns.description: A figure in an I or we sentence. It may be first-hand. Check that it is right and that you could back it up.
patterns.bad: We cut costs by 40%.
patterns.better: We cut costs from [amount] to [amount], measured over [time span].
patterns.fix: Add the time span and what was measured.

patterns.name: Fact from the source is missing
patterns.description: A number, date, name or link is in your notes but not in the draft.
patterns.bad: Notes: 15,000 subscribers. Draft: lots of subscribers.
patterns.better: Carry the detail over from your notes if it matters to the reader.
patterns.fix: Check whether the detail was dropped on purpose.

patterns.name: New figure or link without support
patterns.description: A figure or link is in the draft but in none of the sources, and the sentence has no citation. Typical of invented details.
patterns.bad: Notes: no figure. Draft: 73% of readers stay longer.
patterns.better: Only use figures from your notes, or add the source.
patterns.fix: Check and source the detail, or cut it. Open links and check that they support the claim.

patterns.name: New name or date
patterns.description: A name or date is in the draft but in none of the sources.
patterns.bad: Notes: a client in Leeds. Draft: client Mary Hollis in Leeds.
patterns.better: Stay with the detail from your notes: [as in your notes].
patterns.fix: Check that the name or date is right.

patterns.name: In today's fast-paced world
patterns.bad: In today's fast-paced world, every minute counts.
patterns.better: Since [month/year], we answer requests within [your time span].
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: In the digital age
patterns.description: Era label instead of a concrete trigger.
patterns.bad: In the digital age, everything changes.
patterns.better: Since [concrete change], teams have to [concrete consequence].
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: Ever-evolving landscape
patterns.bad: In the ever-evolving landscape of SEO, ...
patterns.better: Name the one change that affects your readers.
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: Now more than ever
patterns.bad: Visibility matters now more than ever.
patterns.better: Say what changed and when.
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: It's important to note
patterns.description: Announces a point instead of making it.
patterns.bad: It's important to note that backups take time.
patterns.better: Backups take time: plan [your duration] for them.
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: It's no secret that
patterns.description: Claims common knowledge instead of showing it.
patterns.bad: It's no secret that customers read reviews.
patterns.better: Customers read reviews: [what they ask you about first].
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: Delve into
patterns.bad: Let's delve into the details.
patterns.better: Cut the sentence and start with the first detail.
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: Let's dive in
patterns.bad: Let's dive in.
patterns.better: Cut it and start.
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: Welcome to the world of

patterns.better: Open with the question that brought the reader here.
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: Imagine a world

patterns.better: Tell a real case: [what happened to one of your clients].

match.pattern: \bimagine (?:a world|a scenario|this|that|for a moment|if you could)\b

patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: In this article, you'll learn
patterns.description: Table of contents instead of content.
patterns.bad: In this article, you'll learn everything about taxes.
patterns.better: Give the most important answer in the first sentence.

match.pattern: \bin this (?:article|post|blog post|guide|piece),? (?:you['’]ll|you will|we['’]ll|we will|we|you|i['’]ll|i will) (?:learn|explore|discover|look|dive|cover|take a look|walk|break down|examine)\b

patterns.better: In finance, ...

patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: At the end of the day

patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.better: Name the CRM and why it fits.
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.bad: It goes without saying that quality matters.

patterns.name: In a world where

patterns.name: Unprecedented / transformative
patterns.bad: An unprecedented, transformative shift.

patterns.better: It saves time and money.

patterns.description: Must-have words, often without a reason.
patterns.bad: A newsletter is essential.

patterns.name: Dynamic

patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.better: Name the two main benefits.

match.pattern: \b(?:numerous|countless|a wide range of|a wealth of|a host of) (?:benefits|advantages|options|features|opportunities|possibilities)\b

patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: Make a difference
patterns.bad: Small details make all the difference.
patterns.better: Name the detail and what it changed.
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: Increasingly important
patterns.bad: Reviews are increasingly important.
patterns.better: Say how you notice reviews matter more.
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: Optimal results
patterns.bad: Get optimal results.
patterns.better: Name the result you expect.
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: In essence / Essentially
patterns.bad: In essence, it is about trust.
patterns.better: Say what the trust rests on.
patterns.fix: Cut it or replace it with a concrete statement.

patterns.name: Contrast template
patterns.description: "It's not X. It's Y." and similar set-ups that invent a position only to knock it down. Once is a hint, twice is a pattern.
patterns.bad: It's not about reach. It's about trust.
patterns.better: Trust brings us more enquiries than reach: [your observation].
patterns.fix: Drop the straw position and argue your point directly.

patterns.name: Stacked lists of three
patterns.description: Three items in a row again and again ("fast, simple and secure"). One is normal, many sound mechanical.
patterns.bad: Fast, simple and secure. Clear, precise and accessible.
patterns.better: Name only the quality you can back up, and back it up.
patterns.fix: Shorten the lists: two items, or one with evidence.

patterns.name: Connector at the start of a sentence
patterns.description: Repeated sentence openers like "Moreover", "Furthermore", "Additionally". They stack rather than connect.
patterns.bad: Moreover, it is cheap. Furthermore, it is fast.
patterns.better: It is cheap and fast because [reason].
patterns.fix: Cut the connector or state the relation (because, so, but).

patterns.name: Same sentence openings
patterns.description: Three or more sentences in a row start with the same word.
patterns.bad: You plan. You write. You check.
patterns.better: Vary the openings or turn the steps into a list.
patterns.fix: Vary the openings or merge the sentences.

patterns.name: Rhetorical question as opener
patterns.description: A paragraph opens with a question it answers itself right away. Once is fine, repeated it reads like a template.
patterns.bad: Why does this matter? Because customers compare.
patterns.better: Customers compare before they get in touch: [how you notice].
patterns.fix: Write the answer as the first sentence.

patterns.name: Colon reveal
patterns.description: A short lead-in with a colon or question mark builds fake suspense ("The result:", "The reason?").
patterns.bad: The result? More enquiries.
patterns.better: We got more enquiries afterwards, about [your number] a week instead of [before].
patterns.fix: Build a normal sentence: subject, verb, claim.

patterns.name: Grand closing line
patterns.description: The last sentence ends with a grand gesture ("The future is yours", "The first step starts today").
patterns.bad: The future belongs to those who act now.
patterns.better: End with a concrete next step: [what the reader can do tomorrow].
patterns.fix: Cut the closing line or replace it with a concrete step.

patterns.name: Summary ending
patterns.description: The text ends by repeating itself ("In summary", "All in all").
patterns.bad: In summary, planning is important.
patterns.better: End with an open question from your practice or the next step.
patterns.fix: Cut the closing paragraph or replace it with something new.

patterns.name: Trailing participle clause
patterns.description: A sentence gets an interpretation tacked on at the end (", highlighting ...", ", underscoring ...").
patterns.bad: Revenue rose, highlighting the importance of SEO.
patterns.better: Revenue rose. Most of it came from [your source of enquiries].
patterns.fix: Cut the tail or turn it into its own sentence with evidence.

patterns.name: Short sentences
patterns.description: Average words per sentence. Generated expert texts have markedly shorter sentences on average than the human texts in the comparison band.
patterns.bad: Every sentence is short. Every sentence ends fast. No thought develops.
patterns.better: Join thoughts that belong together into one sentence and give the reason [because ...].
patterns.fix: Only a hint: a single value outside the band is common in human texts too. It counts only in combination (R-10).

patterns.name: Uniform sentence lengths
patterns.description: Spread of sentence lengths within paragraphs (coefficient of variation). Very even sentences sit on the generated-text side.
patterns.bad: All sentences have about the same length and shape.
patterns.better: Mix short and long sentences, the way you talk.
patterns.fix: Only a hint: a single value outside the band is common in human texts too. It counts only in combination (R-10).

patterns.name: Short paragraphs
patterns.description: Average words per paragraph. Generated texts split content into many short paragraphs.
patterns.bad: One paragraph, one sentence. Then the next paragraph.
patterns.better: Merge paragraphs that carry one thought together.
patterns.fix: Only a hint: a single value outside the band is common in human texts too. It counts only in combination (R-10).

patterns.name: High vocabulary variety
patterns.description: Vocabulary variety (MATTR, 50-word window). Generated texts repeat words less often and switch synonyms more than human texts.
patterns.bad: Solution, approach, method, strategy: four words for one thing.
patterns.better: Keep the technical term when you mean the same thing.
patterns.fix: Only a hint: a single value outside the band is common in human texts too. It counts only in combination (R-10).

patterns.name: Long words
patterns.description: Average word length in letters. Generated texts reach for long, abstract words more often.
patterns.bad: Operational efficiencies are strategically maximised.
patterns.better: Say what gets faster: [process].
patterns.fix: Only a hint: a single value outside the band is common in human texts too. It counts only in combination (R-10).

patterns.name: Nominal style
patterns.bad: The implementation of the optimisation follows the assessment.
patterns.better: We optimise after we have assessed [object].
patterns.fix: Only a hint: a single value outside the band is common in human texts too. It counts only in combination (R-10).

patterns.name: Many lists of three
patterns.description: Lists of the form "A, B and C" per 1,000 words. Adds a measured rate to pattern T-02.
patterns.bad: Fast, secure and simple. Clear, precise and accessible.
patterns.better: Name only what is true, even if it is two things.
patterns.fix: Only a hint: a single value outside the band is common in human texts too. It counts only in combination (R-10).

patterns.name: Many colons
patterns.description: Colons in running text per 1,000 words (not times or links).
patterns.bad: The goal: growth. The path: clarity. The result: success.
patterns.better: Write full sentences instead of "term: explanation".
patterns.fix: Only a hint: a single value outside the band is common in human texts too. It counts only in combination (R-10).

patterns.name: Trailing participles (rate)
patterns.description: Clauses like ", ensuring ..." or ", making ..." per 1,000 words. Adds a measured rate to pattern T-09.
patterns.bad: We review every text, ensuring the highest quality.
patterns.better: We review every text because [reason].
patterns.fix: Only a hint: a single value outside the band is common in human texts too. It counts only in combination (R-10).

patterns.name: Many measurements on the AI side
patterns.description: At least as many measured features as the band's verdict limit sit outside the band on the generated-text side at the same time. A single feature is only a hint, the combination is a finding.
patterns.bad: Short sentences, short paragraphs, many colons and lists of three in one text.
patterns.better: Rewrite in your own structure: fewer subheadings, longer thoughts, concrete examples [from your work].
patterns.fix: Work on the reported measurements one by one, not just swapping words.

patterns.name: Em dash
patterns.description: Style rule: the em dash (U+2014) outside quotations. Many readers see long dashes as typical of AI. In our measurements it does not separate human from generated text, so it is a style rule you can switch off (config "dashes").
patterns.bad: The result — more enquiries.
patterns.better: The result: more enquiries.
patterns.fix: Replace it with a period, comma, colon or parentheses.

patterns.name: En dash used as a dash
patterns.description: The en dash (U+2013) is right between numbers (10–20); between words it works as a dash.
patterns.bad: Fast – and cheap.
patterns.better: Fast and cheap.
patterns.fix: Replace it with a comma, period or colon.

patterns.name: Hyphen used as a dash
patterns.description: " - " with spaces stands in for a dash.
patterns.bad: Fast - and cheap.
patterns.better: Fast and cheap.
patterns.fix: Replace it with a comma, period or colon.

patterns.name: Emojis
patterns.description: Emojis in expert text. Default: more than one per section is a hint. With emojis: no, each one is a finding.
patterns.bad: 🚀 Start now 💪
patterns.better: Start now.
patterns.fix: Remove the emoji.

patterns.name: Bold overload
patterns.description: Many bold passages in one paragraph. When everything is emphasised, nothing is.
patterns.bad: **Important:** Use **clear** goals and **measurable** values.
patterns.better: Use clear goals and measurable values. Bold at most the one term readers need to find again.
patterns.fix: Reduce bold to one term per section.

patterns.name: Label heading
patterns.description: Headings like "What is X?", "Conclusion" or "Introduction" say where you are, not what you learn.
patterns.bad: ## Conclusion
patterns.better: ## What to change first tomorrow
patterns.fix: Rewrite the heading as a statement or promise.

patterns.name: Too many headings
patterns.description: Many headings for little text. The text breaks into fragments.
patterns.bad: A new subheading every 60 words.
patterns.better: Merge sections until each one has something to say.
patterns.fix: Merge sections.

patterns.name: Banned word (your list)
patterns.description: A word from your own banned list (option --forbid or forbid in .slopcheck.json).
patterns.bad: [a word from your list]
patterns.better: [your preferred wording]
patterns.fix: Replace or cut the word.
